pageCache.text:
Welcome to Oakfields
Oakfields Preparatory School is a school where anything is possible. A place where children are encouraged to dream big, follow their curiosity, and grow in the confidence to take on any challenge.
Oakfields Preparatory School is a thriving independent day school in Upminster for children aged 2½ to 11, where high expectations, exceptional pastoral care and a passion for innovation combine to create an outstanding educational experience. Driven by our vision of Learning Beyond Walls and Aspiring Beyond Limits, we provide children with a broad, ambitious and enriched curriculum that extends far beyond the traditional classroom. From outdoor learning and enterprise projects to sport, performing arts and leadership opportunities, we inspire curiosity, creativity and confidence in every pupil. At Oakfields, we believe that education is about developing the whole child. Our small class sizes, strong family partnerships and nurturing community enable every pupil to be known, valued and challenged to reach their full potential. As we continue to invest in exciting learning environments and curriculum innovation, this is an exceptional opportunity to join a forward-thinking school where staff are empowered to make a genuine difference and contribute to a culture of excellence, ambition and opportunity.
At Oakfields, our children are at the heart of everything we do – and they are, without question, our greatest ambassadors. Every day, they demonstrate the confidence to explore new ideas, the resilience to overcome challenges, and the ambition to pursue their dreams.
Our role is to nurture these qualities, guiding each child to grow not only in knowledge and skills but also in character and values. We believe education is about preparing children for life – helping them become compassionate, curious, and confident individuals who are ready to make a positive impact in the world.
“I am immensely proud of our school, our dedicated staff, and above all, our pupils. When they leave Oakfields, they do so not only ready for their next step, but equipped to embrace the opportunities ahead with courage, kindness, and a belief that they truly can achieve anything.”
- Matthew Booth, Headteacher
A setting that inspires learning.
Housed in a Grade II-listed mansion and set within seven acres of picturesque grounds, our school offers a setting that is both inspiring and welcoming. Outside, our three-acre front field is a daily hub of activity, from playtime to P.E. lessons in rugby, rounders, athletics, and cross-country running. We’re also proud to offer our pupils the use of an on-site swimming pool, where they can build water confidence and develop their skills from an early age. The historic charm of the main house is woven into everyday school life, with many of its original features still in place. Our library provides a calm space to discover new worlds through books, while our versatile hall brings the whole school together. At Oakfields, every space has a purpose: to nurture learning, spark imagination, and give children the belief that anything is possible.
Academic Excellence at every phase.
At Oakfields, academic excellence begins the moment a child joins us and grows with them every step of the way. Our enriched curriculum, often working a year ahead, nurtures curiosity, builds strong foundations, and encourages children to aim high from the very start. By the time they reach Year 6, our pupils are confident, independent learners with a genuine love of discovery. Many secure places at some of the country’s leading senior schools, equipped to embrace new challenges, think creatively, and approach problems with resilience. We’re proud of their achievements at every stage, but even prouder of the people they become.
Our Sustainability Journey
At Oakfields, we believe in nurturing not just brilliant minds, but caring hearts for our planet. Planet Oak is our whole-school commitment to sustainability - a way of thinking, learning and living that places our Earth at the heart of everything we do. From the tiniest hands in Kindergarten to our oldest pupils in Year 6, we're all changemakers, working together for a healthier school and a thriving planet. Every small step counts, and every voice matters.
Come and discover Oakfields
The best way to understand what makes Oakfields so special is to experience it for yourself. Come and see our school in action, meet our teachers, and talk to our pupils - the very best ambassadors for what we do.
Our Exceptional Nursery.
At Oakfields, we believe that a child's first steps into education should be filled with joy, curiosity, and a deep sense of belonging. Our vibrant Nursery, nestled within our dedicated Early Years Village, offers a safe and happy space where children can explore, play, and begin their learning journey with confidence. These early years are a time of wonder and discovery - making friends, trying new things, and beginning to understand the world beyond home. In our nurturing environment, every child is encouraged to be curious, confident, and proud of who they are. We lay the foundations not just for academic success, but for a lifelong love of learning.
A unique learning experience.
An education as individual as every child, inspiring confidence, curiosity, and compassion every day.

Aims, Values & History
Together, we are more than a school - we are Oakfields.
A community with the warmth of family and the ambition of excellence. At Oakfields Preparatory School, community sits at the heart of everything we do. We believe that when children feel known, nurtured, and inspired, they flourish; both academically and personally. Our commitment to Learning Beyond Walls ensures that education stretches far beyond the traditional classroom. Through a broad, balanced, and enriched curriculum, pupils embrace meaningful experiences that spark curiosity, build confidence, and foster a lifelong love of learning. From hands on exploration to real world problem solving, our ever evolving enrichment programme allows every child to discover their passions and pursue them with purpose. We encourage our pupils to Aspire Beyond Limits. Our leadership programme empowers children to develop character, resilience, and the courage to make thoughtful choices. By nurturing future role models, we instil values that endure long after their time with us. Rooted in the heart of Upminster, Oakfields is proud of its history as an Essex based community school. Yet our connection to the wider Blenheim Schools family extends our reach and strengthens our vision, giving pupils access to broader opportunities while preserving the warm, family centred ethos that makes Oakfields unique.
Giving your child an exceptional start.
Come and discover Oakfields Preparatory School.
Our Aims
At Oakfields Preparatory School, we combine the warmth of family with the ambition of excellence, placing community at the heart of all we do. The following aims reflect our commitment to inspiring learning, nurturing character, and empowering every child to aspire beyond limits.
Celebrate individual strengths. We recognise and celebrate every child’s unique talents by offering a broad, balanced, and enriched curriculum that gives every learner space to shine.
Promote an Inclusive Culture & Inter Personal Growth. We build an environment where diversity is celebrated, acceptance is modelled, and interpersonal skills flourish — enabling all children to feel valued and supported.
Develop Curiosity & Global Awareness. We encourage inquisitiveness and praise curiosity, helping children understand the world around them and the global changes shaping their future.
Instil Motivation & Self Belief in Every Child. We cultivate personal goals, champion ambition, and promote strong self belief so every child understands that they can aspire beyond limits.
We nurture confidence by celebrating each child’s unique talents and strengths through a broad and balanced curriculum. We encourage children to set and achieve their own goals, fostering resilience and a strong sense of self.
We foster an inclusive culture that celebrates diversity, promoting acceptance and the development of interpersonal skills to create an environment where every child feels valued and supported.
We nurture curiosity and a passion for learning, empowering children to understand and engage with global changes, cultivating a lifelong love of learning and exploration.
We promote collaboration and community engagement, enabling children to communicate confidently and respectfully in all situations, building strong relationships within the school and beyond.
Exciting Milestones on Our Journey
Oakfields Preparatory School was founded by Mrs Kerrie Malandreniotisas a Day Nursery in Gidea Park. What began as a small early years setting quickly grew into a community built on care, curiosity, and ambition.
The age range expanded to include infants and juniors, and the school moved to Harwood Hall, Upminster. This marked the beginning of Oakfields as a full preparatory school rooted in the local community.
Oakfields continued to grow, starting with just a handful of classes and an ambitious dream: to create a nurturing, adventurous, family centred school where every child could thrive. These early years laid the foundations for the vibrant, forward looking community we are today.
A landmark moment: Oakfields becomes a two form enry school from Reception to Year 6. This milestone reflects our increasing popularity and strong community reputation, marking an exciting evolution from those few classrooms in 2007 into a thriving, dynamic school filled with opportunity.
Oakfields proudly becomes part of the Blenheim Schools family, strengthening our vision, resources, and reach while maintaining our unique identity at the heart of Upminster. This year also saw the launch of the Rainforest Room - a dedicated wellbeing space created to support emotional growth, reflection, and pastoral care.
Our school continues to evolve with specialist environments designed to inspire curiosity, creativity and adventurous learning including: The Build Barn - a bespoke Art, Design & Technology studio for creativity, making, and innovation. The Discovery Barn - a dedicated Science and Food Technology space where pupils can experiment, explore, and tackle real world problems. Little Oak's Farm - a unique outdoor learning and sustainability project, preparing for its first crop in 2027.
Come and discover Oakfields Preparatory School.
Where exceptional learning takes place day to day.

Sport and Music
Unleashing Potential
At Oakfields, music and sport are part of our heartbeat, helping children grow in confidence, creativity and character.
Music is taught from Pre-Prep upwards, giving pupils the chance to explore everything from ukuleles and keyboards to hand-held percussion and instruments from around the world. It’s all about inspiring a love of music that will last a lifetime.
Our ‘sport for all’ approach means every child gets the opportunity to take part, try something new and feel the buzz of being part of a team. We host regular fixtures with other schools and work with partners including JW Tennis, Chelsea Football Club and Sabrina Mercury Swimming School to broaden our pupils’ skills.
Whether playing a melody or a sport, every child is supported to try new things, grow their abilities and find joy in what they do.
Sporting champions
From Nursery upwards, pupils take part in a wide range of activities, from swimming in our heated indoor pool to football, tennis, athletics and more. Lessons, led by specialist teachers, focus on developing skills, teamwork and strategic thinking, while fostering confidence and a love of being active. We’re proud of our strong sporting tradition – many pupils go on to earn scholarships at leading independent schools. Highlights include our summer Sports Day, fixtures with other schools, and an exciting choice of sport-related clubs that keep children engaged all year round.

Nurturing a lifelong love for movement
PE at Oakfields is all about inspiring a love for movement from the very start. Through engaging games and challenges, pupils develop key skills, confidence and a positive approach to being active. As they progress, children have opportunities to push themselves further, build leadership skills and excel in their chosen sports. Many go on to achieve success at county and national levels, with alumni often sharing how their time at Oakfields set the foundations for their achievements.
Instrumental excellence
Alongside curriculum music, pupils can choose to learn an instrument with our talented team of specialist peripatetic teachers. From strings and piano to singing for musical theatre, guitar (classical and rock) and drums, there is something to inspire every budding musician. Children are encouraged to work towards graded exams with leading examination boards, celebrating their progress and achievements along the way. Our whole school choir meets weekly and our musicians perform throughout the year at assemblies, concerts, and special occasions like our much-loved Christmas Carol Concert.
Music curriculum
Music at Oakfields is carefully planned and taught by our dedicated music specialist, ensuring every child’s journey is inspiring from the very start. From the age of three, pupils explore songs, actions and activities that link closely to their learning in Nursery, building confidence and joy in music-making. From Reception onwards, the curriculum grows with them, introducing skills such as reading music, playing instruments including the recorder, ukulele and keyboards, and experimenting with musical improvisation to spark creativity.
An example of how our key principles, Pitch and Rhythm, are used throughout our curriculum is provided below, showcasing how they are built upon and integrated throughout the curriculum:
Our children are introduced to the concept of very basic ideologies of music through music and movement, where they learn to recognise high and low pitches and respond to them in specific ways. They also explore stemmed rhythmic notation, recognising crotchet beats and their corresponding sounds.
Children are introduced to dot notation and the concept of high, middle and low using glockenspiels. They create their own pitch patterns and learn to read given pitch patterns. Throughout the unit focused on rhythm, they begin to explore crotchets and quavers (Ta and Ti-ti) by creating their own rhythms and reading basic rhythms by sight.
The idea of high and low becomes an introduction to the tonic sol-fa system where children are shown the first 3 pitches of a scale (Do, Re, Mi) and they use hand movements to pitch, sing and recognise the sounds. We continue to explore rhythm by sight reading and playing along to a drumbeat!
Rhythmic notation is further explored as children create music using London underground tube stops to form patterns. They are given autonomy to compose, notate, and perform their own underground raps. Building on their knowledge of Do, Re, Mi, they begin to learn pitched notation and start playing the recorder.
Traditional songs and the pentatonic scale are explored, with students using their understanding of pitch to work out traditional songs by ear. They create their own pentatonic pieces, incorporating their understanding of pitch and rhythm. The recorder unit is revisited, with a focus on developing a more challenging repertoire of pieces.
The first unit focuses on rhythmic patterns, exploring ostinato pieces and composing, notating, and performing their own pieces inspired by "Connect it" by Anna Meredith from Ten Pieces. Students also use their knowledge of notation and pitch to create improvisations around melodies inspired by Chinese New Year, the Blues, and participate in whole-class performances.
In their final year, students integrate their knowledge by exploring rhythmic ostinatos in a unit that examines the music and themes of Harry Potter. They also analyse and create cover versions of their own choice of music. Additionally, they explore becoming a class band and collaborate on putting together a piece of music as a class.

With our staff providing expert guidance along the way, children develop genuine self-confidence, learn to express themselves clearly, and build skills that will serve them well - whether through sport, music, drama, clubs, or any of our other inspiring activities.

Careers at Oakfields
Oakfields Preparatory School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff, volunteers and third parties to share this commitment. Safer recruitment practice and pre-employment checks will be undertaken before any appointment is confirmed. Inspection Reports
Inspection Reports
2025 ISI Inspection Summary
INSPECTION REPORT: 2025
Exceptional Standards
This inspection was conducted under the new ISI framework introduced in 2023, which assesses schools across five key areas. We are very pleased to share that Oakfields met all standard. 1. Leadership, management, and governance 2. Quality of education 3. Pupils’ physical and mental health and emotional wellbeing 4. Pupils’ social and economic education 5. Safeguarding
INSPECTION REPORT: 2022
Excellent in every area
Our 2022 inspection evaluated two key areas at Oakfields. The regulatory compliance assessment looked at our standards on safeguarding, health and safety, suitability of staff, provision of information, handling of complaints and leadership - and we were found to be fully compliant in all areas. The educational quality review examined our pupils' achievement and development, our school ethos and the exceptional experience we deliver from Nursery to Year 6 - achieving an excellent judgement across every area.
INSPECTION REPORT: 2015 and 2019
Excellent in every area
In 2015 and 2019, Oakfields received a Regulatory Compliance Inspection where we met the standards in the schedule to the Education Regulations 2014, following lesson observations, examining samples of pupils’ work and formal interviews with staff, pupils and governors.

Oakfields prepares pupils extensively, yet supportively, to achieve a place at their first choice Senior School. We are proud of the solid foundation we give our pupils before they progress to new Senior Schools. Despite being non-selective, our pupils go on to achieve places at some of the best Grammar and Independent Schools in the region, including the offer of scholarships.
Destination Schools
Yearly insight
Proud of our children's journey to success.
We take great pride in the success our children in Key Stage 2 obtain, with the majority of our children gaining access to their first choice school. We accurately predict a child’s suitability to a wide range of senior schools and give parents guidance on the schools that will be right for their child. Our close working relationship with many of these schools helps inform our discussion with parents. From Year 4 upwards, children who intend to apply for local Grammar Schools are offered assistance with selective examinations and interviews.

What do our alumni say about their time at Oakfields Preparatory School?
"The children at Oakfields are really lucky to have such a great start to school life. There is a positive, encouraging, friendly and family feel all around the school and after all they have done for me, it certainly made an easier (and not so scary) transition to my chosen Senior school, especially in the preparation for my exam and interview."
"Oakfields prepared me for Brentwood School by opening my eyes to a higher standard of education, after spending my infant years at a state infant school. pageCache.pageTitle: Private Nursery In Upminster, Essex - Oakfields Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Nursery (2½ to 4)
A warm and welcoming Nursery for children.
The formative years of a child’s education are ones of excitement, exploration and discovery, where they will begin to make friends, experience new opportunities and learn about a world beyond the secure confines of their immediate home life. We know and understand that this is a very important time for both you and your child. Our Nursery staff are highly experienced, supportive and caring and are dedicated to helping your child grow in confidence and independence. Each child is given one-to-one teaching and our excellent pupil to staff ratios ensure each child will have activities suited to their unique needs.
Giving your child an exceptional start.
Come and discover Oakfields Preparatory School.
Facilities & Location
The perfect setting for your child to begin their education.
Our children enjoy a huge range of activities and our spacious, purpose-designed Early Years Village offers plenty of green space and endless opportunities for indoor and outdoor free flow play and learning. As well as large classrooms, enclosed playground and outdoor learning area, the children enjoy access to the beautiful adjoining orchard, the extensive grounds and other areas.
Oakfields Early Years Village
Featuring three calm, relaxing classrooms, a wide range of Early Years learning resources, floor to ceiling windows, and access to our Early Years play space and orchard, our Early Years village offers children the very best environment in which to learn, grow and explore.
We are proud to have the Millie’s Mark award.
Oakfields has been awarded Millie’s Mark, a special endorsement that highlights our commitment to going above and beyond in ensuring the safety and wellbeing of children. This achievement reflects the dedication and expertise of our Early Years staff, who have all completed paediatric first aid training and demonstrated competence and confidence in applying it in practice. Beyond meeting the minimum requirements, Millie’s Mark recognises that we have robust procedures and documentation in place, providing parents with even greater reassurance about their children’s safety.
A richly diverse EYFS curriculum.
Our children follow a specifically-tailored and richly diverse EYFS curriculum, flavoured with the many positive influences and ideals of Preparatory teaching, which allows children to grow naturally, retain their individuality and develop their unique personalities. Whilst the curriculum is planned to maximise learning in each of the following seven areas, our ethos is very much to promote cross-curricular learning both indoors and outdoors.
Communication and Language
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Physical Development
Literacy
Expressive Art and Design
Mathematics
Understanding The World
Join our family.
Boys and girls can join our younger Nursery class from the term in which they turn three years of age. They may attend on a 2, 3 or 5-day-a week basis. Attendance in our older Nursery classes progresses to a 5-day-a-week basis, so children are able to benefit from our teaching and learning every day and become used to the routines of school before they progress to Reception. We operate on a first-come, first-served basis and therefore recommend early registration where possible. Gradually, each child builds up a strong sense of independence coupled with an ability to sustain concentration and develop their own thinking. Confidence grows as their range of skills increases, along with a true passion for learning and discovery.
A unique learning experience.
Oakfields Prep is a happy and vibrant independent day school in Upminster, offering a bespoke and holistic education.
Your Child’s Journey Nursery
Oakfields School

pageCache.pageTitle: Preparatory School In Upminster, Essex - Oakfields Prep School
pageCache.text:
Upper-School (8 to 11)
Guidance and care throughout.
During your child’s journey through the Upper School, we aim to give our pupils a diverse and balanced education as they work towards making the transition to secondary school. Children benefit from verbal reasoning lessons to help prepare for the 11+ and independent school entrance exams, as well as assistance with selective examinations and interviews. We celebrate high levels of achievement and ambition and push boundaries, so children go beyond simply the acquisition of knowledge; we want our children to be problem solvers, active learners and generous members of the wider society.
Giving your child an exceptional start.
Come and discover Oakfields Preparatory School.
A richly diverse curriculum
Whilst there is a focus on core subjects, we aim to provide pupils with a diverse and balanced education as they prepare for the transition to secondary school. We strive to foster a love of erudition and create lifelong learners by designing a curriculum that includes a variety of topics and perspectives, reflecting our diverse school community. From Year 4 onwards, all children benefit from Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning lessons to prepare for the 11+ and independent school entrance exams. We also provide assistance with selective examinations and interviews. We offer “Study skills” to teach our children how to structure their independent learning, tailored to support their journey to different destination schools. Throughout Years 4 and 5, both in and out of the classroom, support and guidance are provided to ensure children are well-prepared for these exams. Music and P.E. are integral parts of the curriculum and are taught by specialist teachers, as is Spanish, Swimming and Forest School.
Art & Design
Design Technology
Geography
Religious Education
Verbal/Non-Verbal Reasoning
Study Skills
Current Affairs
1:1 Device Programme
Upper School pupils also benefit from Blenheim School’s 1:1 Device Programme, where every pupil in Years 4-6 is provided with a school-managed laptop for the duration of their education. This supports the development of vital technology skills integrated throughout lessons, not limited to computing classes alone. Additionally, we emphasise the importance of teaching children how to safely and responsibly navigate the digital world.
Learning beyond the classroom.
We believe that education is as much about what happens outside a classroom as what happens within and our extra-curricular activities are a fantastic way for pupils to pursue their interests or try something new. Our children enjoy a range of external trips and internal visitors that enrich the curriculum and bring it to life. Regular themed days and weeks are arranged to allow focus on a particular area or subject and to recognise or celebrate national and world events.
A unique learning experience
An education as individual as every child, inspiring confidence, curiosity, and compassion every day.
Your Child’s Journey Nursery
Oakfields School

Turning Unique Talents Into Remarkable Futures
Everyone is unique. At Blenheim, we recognise all talents and abilities. Nurturing aspirations and building confidence, we accompany each pupil on a deeply personal and ambitious learning journey towards a remarkable future.
A Blenheim Education
An Education With Purpose.For a Life of Possibilities
We know that children learn best when they are happy and engaged. Our schools are vibrant communities built on friendship and kindness. Imagination and playfulness are woven into school life and our diverse curriculum enables pupils to explore new experiences and discover new passions. Education is a precious and exhilarating journey of self-discovery, and we want pupils to thrive socially and emotionally, as well as academically.
We’re here to inspire a lifelong love of learning in every pupil. Through our rich curriculum and highly individualised teaching, we help them develop genuine intellectual curiosity and academic confidence. With life skills embedded into every lesson, pupils are challenged and inspired to think deeply and critically, solve problems and communicate effectively – a solid foundation for their lives ahead.
Nurturing Their Extraordinary
Our classrooms are creative and stimulating places in which to learn. We celebrate effort, welcome debate and see mistakes as part of the journey to improvement. Pupils are encouraged to aim high, rise to the challenge and take pride in their achievements. At the same time, they learn the lifelong value of collaboration, empathy and mutual respect, crucial qualities that will stand them in good stead.
LIFE-READY LEARNERS
The future is complex and fast-changing. Young people need future-ready skills, in addition to strong academic achievement. A successful and fulfilling adulthood is built on a well-rounded education, imbued with moral values, sound judgement and self-discipline grounded in self-worth. A Blenheim education equips them with all of these qualities and many more.
The future is theirs to embrace and the possibilities are endless. Together, let’s make sure they’re ready for it.
Oakfields School

Academic Excellence
Proud of our academic excellence.
As a non-selective independent school, we take great pride in our track record of academic excellence. All of our pupils receive personalised learning and individual attention, instilling a strong work ethic that consistently yields exceptional results. We have an enviable record of success in supporting our pupils to secure places at their first-choice senior schools, including Grammar Schools and top-tiered Independent Secondary Schools.
Giving your child an exceptional start.
Come and discover Oakfields Preparatory School.
Guidance from an early age.
We believe in tracking pupils from an early age, using National Standardised tests in English and Mathematics, among others, to assess the children's progress, monitor their development, and set targets for future attainment. Progress Test in English (PTE) assesses pupils' technical English skills, including spelling, grammar, punctuation, and reading comprehension. The Progress Test in Maths (PTM) monitors their mathematical skills and knowledge in areas such as number, shape, data handling, and algebra, as well as their mathematical reasoning and problem-solving abilities. The results presented below show age-standardised scores, with the orange dashed line indicating the national average of 100. Notably, our pupils have consistently achieved scores significantly above the national average.
Early Years Foundation Stage Profile Results
We’re proud that our EYFS results continue to exceed national and local averages. In 2025–26= 90% of our Reception children achieved a Good Level of Development with consistently strong results over the last several years.
A Good Level of Development (GLD) is awarded to children who meet the Early Learning Goals across the five key areas of the EYFS curriculum: - Personal, Social and Emotional Development - Physical Development - Communication and Language - Literacy - Mathematics These results reflect the strong foundations we lay in our Early Years setting, supporting each child’s growth, confidence and love of learning.
Nurturing a love of learning.
While academic results are vitally important to us at Oakfields, we place equal emphasis on providing a well-rounded education that cultivates enthusiastic, confident, and resilient individuals. Our children leave here as resourceful and enthusiastic individuals, with a love of learning that will sustain them through their school lives and beyond.
Students enter exams confident and well prepared.
Preparation for the 11+ examination begins in Year 2 and progresses systematically throughout a student's educational journey. By the time they reach Year 6 and sit for the exams, students are equipped with confidence and are well-prepared.
From an early age, we prioritise creative writing skills, nurturing and refining them throughout your child's educational path.
Starting from Year 2, students are taught verbal and non-verbal reasoning. These skills are integrated into their regular curriculum subjects and are supplemented by standalone weekly lessons.
While we adopt a holistic approach to curriculum delivery, we ensure regular assessment through weekly tests on times tables and spellings starting from Year 3. Additionally, end-of-term assessments are conducted in exam conditions to familiarise students with the exam environment.
Students receive specialised interview preparation sessions with the Headteacher, Mr. Booth, to excel in the interview component of the 11+ examination.
We utilise Atom School resources to aid students in tackling ISEB-style questioning and to instil proper exam etiquette.
Regular assessments are conducted to hone students' higher order thinking and inference skills, crucial for success in the 11+ examination.
Students act as tour guides to prospective families during Open Events, providing them with valuable experience in communicating with unfamiliar adults.
Oakfields School

Cuffley Active Learning Centre
Cuffley Active Learning Centre.
Cuffley is more than a traditional outdoor activity centre: by fusing the outdoors with the curriculum, it serves as a natural extension of our students’ learning environment. The benefits of the outdoors in supporting health and wellbeing are well documented. At the core of Cuffley’s programmes are fun, adventurous and educational experiences that use the natural environment of our woodlands to support wellbeing, develop character and progress essential skills. The site has also been approved to offer the John Muir Award, a nationally recognised environmental award that sees students working to preserve wildlife and wild places, with students able to attain their Bronze Award via a residential course or through a series of day visits.
Team-building sessions
Outdoor Learning
Resilience and risk-taking scenarios
Climbing walls
High and Low Rope
Learn more about the Cuffley experience.
Accommodation
Accommodation options at Cuffley include camping, a newly created pod village and en-suite indoor bunk rooms. These sit alongside fully equipped classrooms and an impressive central refectory. Contained within an environment of Special Scientific Interest and supported by the highest standard of facilitators, accommodation and nutritious organic food, Cuffley provides a dedicated woodland space, thoughtfully and carefully curated to offer our children a unique and diverse experience that they can take with them into the world ahead.
Oakfields School

Our Community
More than just a school, we are a family.
Oakfields has a strong sense of community and parents and visitors often comment on the friendly and personal atmosphere in the school. The success of our school depends on the unique partnership between staff, children and parents. As a small school, all the children and staff get to know each other quickly on a personal level, creating a real sense of family and community, where every individual is accepted as equal and valued.
Giving your child an exceptional start.
Come and discover Oakfields Preparatory School.
Helping our local community.
We encourage our pupils to play a positive role in contributing to the life of the school and the wider community and, as a school, we actively seek links with the local community.
Participation in Tate Modern Museum’s “Steve McQueen Year 3” exhibition.
Sponsoring and decorating a Christmas tree for Upminster’s Christmas Tree Festival.
Decorating a window with a nativity mural for Romford’s ‘Nativity’ in The Brewery hosted by Romford Elim Church.
Our Year 6 Student Leadership team includes Charity Captains who are dedicated to supporting both local and international charities. Our goal is to foster a community that is not only rooted in local values but also globally aware.
Oakfields PTA
Our Parent Teacher Association (Oakfields PTA) plays an integral role in our school community, enriching our vision and philosophy. Events ranging from Summer Fayres to Movie Nights and School Discos are made possible through their collaboration and support.

pageCache.pageTitle: Why Choose A Prep School? - Oakfields Prep School
pageCache.text:
Pastoral Care & Wellbeing
Nurturing Every Child
At Oakfields, we believe that nurturing both our pupils’ wellbeing and their connection to the world around them is central to a meaningful education.
Wellbeing matters
Every child who walks through our doors deserves to feel seen, safe and heard. At Oakfields, we are united in our commitment to protecting and nurturing each child. We believe that when children feel truly safe, they reach their full potential. That's why we've built our school on foundations of trust, understanding, and genuine care. Our safeguarding practices aren't just policies on paper – they're a living promise that reflects our deep responsibility to every family who entrusts us with their children. Communication is at the heart of everything we do. We want every child to know they have voices that matter and adults who will listen with open hearts. When children feel heard and understood, they grow in confidence and courage. We see parents as our partners in this journey of nurturing young minds and hearts. Together, we create a circle of care that extends from home to school and back again, ensuring that every child feels supported, encouraged, and celebrated wherever they are.
In every classroom, we use the Zones of Regulation to help children identify and manage their emotions, supported by regular check-ins to ensure every child feels seen, heard, and supported. Our playgrounds include dedicated wellbeing zones, calm, reflective spaces where pupils can reset, connect with friends, or seek quiet time when needed. Pupil voice is at the heart of what we do. Each year, children apply and are interviewed for key leadership roles such as Wellbeing Captain and Eco Captains, voted for by their peers. These pupil leaders work closely with staff and the wider school community to promote a healthy, sustainable lifestyle.
Wraparound Care at Oakfields
At Oakfields, we are proud to offer our Wraparound Care provision, which includes both Breakfast Club and After School Care, designed to support busy families while providing a safe, nurturing environment for our pupils.
Our Wraparound provision is more than just extended hours – it’s an extension of our school’s ethos of care, support, and enrichment, helping children start and end their day positively.
Breakfast Club runs from 07:30 to 08:15 After School Care operates from 15:00 (depending on your child’s staggered finish time) until 17:45. Your child will be cared for by our dedicated Oakfields staff, who provide not only supervision but also a warm, supportive atmosphere where every child feels valued and secure. We understand the importance of consistency and emotional wellbeing, and our team is committed to fostering positive relationships and a sense of belonging.
During Wraparound Care, children will: Take part in weekly themed activities that encourage creativity, collaboration, and fun. Have the opportunity to complete homework independently (Upper School), with quiet spaces available. Be served a nutritious breakfast in the morning and a light tea with snacks in the afternoon — all included in the cost.
Food is provided at all sessions.
